course_title: Applied AI Agent Architectures: From Conversational Spark to LangGraph Systems
contact_hours_weekly: 300 Minutes (150 min Synchronous Lab + 150 min Asynchronous Guided Study)
description: An accelerated, hands-on exploration of the modern AI Agent spectrum—advancing from prompt-driven conversational models (Gemini Spark, Anthropic Claude) through visual and low-code orchestration engines (n8n, Langflow), to production code-first stateful multi-agent graphs (LangGraph). Students design, prototype, evaluate, and deploy autonomous agents with tool use, memory, human-in-the-loop safeguards, and graph-based control flow.
outcomes: CLO 1 (Agent Taxonomy & Prompt Architectures): Differentiate levels of agent autonomy and implement structured reasoning loops (ReAct, Plan-and-Solve) using foundation models (Google Gemini, Anthropic Claude).
CLO 2 (Visual & Low-Code Orchestration): Construct, debug, and automate multi-step agentic workflows and API integrations using visual platforms (n8n, Langflow).

CLO 3 (Stateful Graph Engineering): Architect cyclical, stateful agent workflows using code-first frameworks (LangGraph), defining typed states, routing nodes, conditional edges, and persistent checkpointers.
CLO 4 (Tool Integration & Action Dispatch): Design and execute robust tool-calling schemas (JSON Schema / Pydantic) with dynamic discovery, parameter validation, and exception fallback handling.
CLO 5 (Human-in-the-Loop & Safety Governance): Implement state interrupts, review breakpoints, permission gating, and rate limiting to ensure secure, deterministic agent behavior.
CLO 6 (Multi-Agent Systems & Evaluation): Coordinate multi-agent collaborative networks (hierarchical supervisors, specialized workers) and benchmark performance via automated evaluation suites.
